title: Coping with pain among adults with chronic tic disorders
study_type: Cross-sectional convenience sample with questionnaires and YGTSS interview
population: 76 adult support-group attendees in Poland, ages 18–51; 57 GTS, 19 CMTD, no chronic vocal tic disorder; no defined severe-persistent-adult subgroup
exposure: Tic-related pain, coping, beliefs and recalled care; no assigned treatment
outcomes: Past-or-present pain;present/worst VAS;Polish SF-MPQ-2,CSQ,BPCQ;combined 0–100 YGTSS;study care questionnaire
followup: No prospective follow-up;YGTSS within one week of paper questionnaire

numeric_results.care_conflict: Help-seeking stated 86% but 19 men + 31 women=50/56=89.29%; 31 women exceeds 30 female pain respondents. Relief 10 labelled 18% of seekers, but 10/56=17.86% and 10/50=20%; corrected denominator unknown
numeric_results.current_worst: Sex-total means yield conditional 2.925 current and 4.3 worst, gap 1.375; not temporal change, inference or accepted corrected estimate. Female worst 4.3 incompatible with 20/10 diagnosis means 4.6/4.2 under ordinary one-decimal rounding.

uncertainty: Reported SDs,medians,ranges,rounded p-values and rho symbols. No CIs for relevant estimands; no invented CIs,covariance,participant outcomes or clinical thresholds. Conditional rounding ranges are not confidence intervals.
negative_findings: No nominal present/worst pain gender difference
No reported significant pain-intensity difference by self-reported depression
No reported coping/YGTSS or BPCQ/pain association
Pain-domain and belief-domain gender contrasts nonsignificant;not equivalence
adverse_events: No assigned intervention or systematic comparative safety estimate; questionnaire offered side-effect reasons but category counts not reported
attrition: Invitations,refusals,item-level missingness and uncertain-response counts unreported
risk_of_bias: Unbounded worst-pain and care recall windows
Inconsistent help counts,percentages and female worst mean
Ambiguous SF-MPQ-2 scoring/denominators and BPCQ raw-score comparability
conflicts_funding: Author reports no research/publication funding or relevant commercial/financial conflicts
applicability: Directly adult but not representative prevalence or severe-adult treatment evidence;does not cover chronic vocal tic disorder
claim_supported: Pain-specific adult burden and unmet-care experience need separately defined outcomes;denominators/time windows materially affect what claims can be made
claim_not_supported: Representative current/chronic pain prevalence,causal care efficacy/inefficacy,self-management superiority,neuropathic diagnosis,severe-adult effect,durable benefit,disease modification or cure
retrieval_status: Primary HTML/PDF,official EuropePMC XML and blank care questionnaire supplement inspected;main PDF pages 3, 4, 6 and both supplement pages visually verified
reviewer: Research assistant;independent source/computation review supplied separately;not clinical peer review
correction_retraction_check: No linked notice in PubMed/Crossref or focused DOI notice search;not comprehensive clearance
next_verification_task: Close unchanged source audit. Next inspect Taylor 2022 DOI 10.3389/fpsyt.2022.914044 for pain-interference ascertainment,entry selection,time windows and adult-specific availability;age 16–71 cannot be assumed adult-only. No outreach or participant access.
privacy: No participant records,quotations,singleton values,family data or full-paper copies in deliverables
